column2: SysV AMD64 v1.0 classifies each argument into INTEGER/SSE classes passes INTEGER args in RDI/RSI/RDX/RCX/R8/R9 and SSE args in XMM0-XMM7; stack arguments are rounded to eightbytes and the end of the caller's input-argument area shall be 16-byte aligned

Windows x64 passes integer arguments in RCX/RDX/R8/R9; requires the caller to allocate a 32-byte shadow store; and passes by reference any argument not 1/2/4/8 bytes (including 16-byte types); varargs require FP values duplicated in GP registers
column10: Diverges from SysV on >8-byte structs and varargs

column2: AAPCS64 (2025Q4) requires SP mod 16 = 0 (quad-word aligned); passes HFAs/HVAs of at most 4 members in SIMD registers; and defines long double as IEEE 754-2008 quad precision

RISC-V psABI flattens aggregates field-by-field into at most two registers; never flattens unions; and explicitly marks ILP32E as unstable and RV64ILP32* as experimental (stack pointer need only be 32-bit aligned there)
column10: psABI master is a 2.0-rc0 draft — ABI still moving

column2: long double diverges across mainstream targets: 80-bit x87 extended (16-byte storage) on SysV x86-64 LP64 vs IEEE-754 quad on AArch64; C11 leaves its characteristics implementation-defined
column10: Any C-FFI type mapping must special-case it

column2: va_list is a target-specific data structure (SysV: a 4-field struct; RISC-V requires register-passed and stack-passed varargs to share memory-layout ordering for va_arg)

C11 defines a data race as conflicting non-atomic actions without happens-before and gives such races undefined behavior; programs using mutexes and seq_cst behave as if simply interleaved (DRF guarantee)
The C++11 memory model as specified was not correctly implementable on Power and ARM for combined acquire/release + seq_cst code; WG21 revised the model in P0668R5 (shipped in C++20)
column10: Paper cites Lahav et al. SCFix

column2: WG21 states memory_order_consume is widely acknowledged to be unusable and implementations treat it as acquire; C11 (N1570) still standardizes memory_order_consume
column10: Conflict between WG21 (2018) and WG14 FDIS text (2011); in conflicting-evidence.md

column2: Modern x86 multiprocessors are TSO not sequentially consistent: the store-buffering litmus (SB) can end with both processors reading 0 without fences
ARMv8's public memory model was originally non-multicopy-atomic but was simplified to multicopy-atomic (Arm co-authored POPL'18 model); RISC-V RVWMO is likewise specified as other-multi-copy-atomic
column10: Weak models are converging on multi-copy atomicity

column2: RISC-V requires LR/SC addresses to be naturally aligned and guarantees atomic execution only for naturally aligned loads/stores; misaligned accesses may trap or be non-atomic
column10: Alignment is a semantic requirement not just a perf hint

column2: The RISC-V Atomics ABI requires C/C++-style atomic mappings to interoperate across languages in one process and warns that naive mapping combinations fail to enforce seq_cst store followed by seq_cst load ordering
column10: Per-ISA atomics ABI conformance is needed not just codegen

column2: MSVC volatile semantics are selected by flag and target: /volatile:iso gives no acquire/release guarantees (default on ARM); /volatile:ms adds them but forces hardware memory barriers; Microsoft recommends /volatile:iso plus explicit synchronization
Practitioner and kernel documentation record unaligned access as a genuine portability axis: behaviour varies by architecture (exception/crash or large slowdown)

C11 freestanding environments leave program startup; termination and available library facilities implementation-defined beyond a minimal header set; bare-metal Rust links core instead of std and drops the std runtime
column10: The normative pattern for no-OS language cores

column2: GNU ld's linker scripts let the program owner set the entry point (ENTRY); section layout (SECTIONS) and ELF program headers (PHDRS); OS and embedded work depends on this link-time layout control
Documented ABI breaks occur even in the most conservative ecosystems: GCC 5.1 shipped a parallel C++11 libstdc++ ABI and glibc changed the s390 jmp_buf size (2.19) managed via symbol versioning

Hypothesis: Kavir should fix the portable core (fixed integer widths; explicit endianness conversion; explicit alignment requirements; only acquire/release/seq_cst atomics; race semantics that are not UB) and confine per-target struct-passing; va_list; long double and vector ABI details to a documented repr/FFI layer

Hypothesis: Kavir's freestanding tier should require an explicit entry point; a mandatory panic/abort handler and no runtime services mirroring C11 freestanding + Rust no_std with memory layout delegated to linker directives
